title: Who Really Pays the Tariff? The Fed's Own Research Has an Answer
summary: Explainer on New York Fed findings that Americans, not foreigners, pay tariffs, and that court-ordered refunds went to importers while consumers got nothing.

assertions.quote: the promise was simple. Foreigners pay. China pays, Mexico pays, not you. Well, the receipts are in now, and they tell a very different story.
the tariff is collected from the American importer, not the foreign company
About a third comes from goods made right here in America
about 1/4 of a tariff increase ends up passed through to consumer goods prices. Not all of it, roughly a quarter.
tariffs added 2.9 percentage points to consumer goods inflation, peaking this February
The inflation shock cools, but prices do not come back down. The damage is baked into the level.
There's no mechanism to refund a higher grocery bill.

verdicts.note: Customs refunds duties to the importer of record; there is no legal or practical channel to return them to retail buyers.

assertions.quote: One that lands hardest on the people with the least room to absorb it.
